Wyoming property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • Residential property is assessed at 9.5% of market value; taxable value is a percent of fair market value, 9.5% for all other property, 11.5% for industrial. (W.S. 39-11-101(a)(xvii); source)
  • An assessment appeal is filed with the county assessor no later than 30 days after the date of the assessment schedule notice, stating why the assessment is incorrect. (W.S. 39-13-109(b)(i); source)
  • The county board of equalization hears the appeal and may affirm the assessor's valuation or find for the taxpayer and remand; written findings are due by October 1 each year. (W.S. 39-13-109(b)(i); source)
  • A taxpayer may appeal a county board of equalization decision to the State Board of Equalization within 30 days of entry of the decision or its legal postmark mailing date, whichever is later. (Dept. of Revenue - Residential (Appeal Process); source)
  • The appeal must address market value, not the tax rate, and must include evidence supporting the owner's estimate of market value. (Dept. of Revenue - Residential (Appeal Process); source)
  • An order of the State Board of Equalization may be appealed to the district court of the county where the property is located. (W.S. 39-13-109(b)(iv); source)
  • An action to enjoin an illegal assessment, levy or collection must be filed in district court within one year following the illegal assessment, levy or collection. (W.S. 39-13-109(c)(i); source)
  • The county treasurer advertises a real property tax sale once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, first publication at least four weeks before the sale. (W.S. 39-13-108(e)(ii)(A); source)
  • Sales are held at the county courthouse between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.; the person offering to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is the purchaser and receives a certificate of purchase. (W.S. 39-13-108(e)(iii); source)
